confirmed.description: The Fisherman's face changes. In both carry panels he is drawn plumper and younger, with a heavy black curled handlebar moustache, black curly hair and only light grey stubble on the chin. This is not the lean, grizzled, short-full-beard leader established in 2.1 and 2.2 and held in 3.4, 4.2 and 4.5. Squeezed beside Nagoji, he reads as a second curly-haired man with a curled moustache rather than the same fisherman.
confirmed.evidence: 5.1, left figure (red lungi, white shoulder cloth, holding Nagoji's shoulders): a thick black upturned moustache dominates the face, and the chin shows only a small grey patch. 5.2, figure behind Nagoji at left: the same heavy black moustache on a round, nearly clean-cheeked face, under black hair. Compare 2.1 (top-left face on page 2): a full short grey-and-black beard covers his cheeks and chin, and his strong white teeth show. Only the red lungi and white cloth tie him to the earlier panels.

verdict.reason: The face drift is real, but it is minor, not major. Zoomed crops of 5.1 (left carrier) and 5.2 (carrier behind Nagoji) show a heavy black moustache. The grey is cut back to a stubble patch on the chin and jaw, and the cheeks are mostly bare. That differs from the short grizzled beard over cheeks and chin in 2.1, 2.2, 3.4, 4.2 and 4.5, which 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5 on this same page also keep. Script 2.1 asks for the three faces to be held for the whole chapter, so this is a genuine slip. The reviewer overstates it, though. The heavy black moustache is not new: 4.2 already gives him the same thick black moustache over the grey beard. He keeps the black curly hair from 2.1, and he still has visible grey on the chin, so he still reads as an older man with a grizzled chin. He also keeps the red lungi and the white cloth on his left shoulder. He carries Nagoji's shoulders exactly as in 4.5, the panel just before, so the beat-to-beat continuity tells the reader who he is. At print size his face in 5.1 and 5.2 is only about 0.3 inch tall. The missing cheek beard is a fine detail there, and nothing in either panel would make a reader take him for someone else or confuse him with Nagoji, who stays distinct in the ochre tunic, slung between the carriers. So this is a polish fix: if these panels are regenerated, restore the short grey beard on his cheeks. It does not need a forced redraw.

confirmed.description: The brand is on the wrong arm. Nagoji's chest faces the camera and his head is up, so the arm hanging down on the Fisherman's side (image left) is his RIGHT arm. That forearm carries the red ridged brand pattern just above the bandaged wrist. His left hand is the one gripping the Fisherman's forearm across his chest. Bible ch4 row and script: the brand is on the inner LEFT forearm only.
confirmed.evidence: page-04.png, original px ~(430-560, 2050-2300): the hanging bandaged arm beside the red lungi shows branching red raised marks above the wrist wrap. 4.3 correctly puts the same mark on the image-right (left) forearm.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. In panel 4.5 on page 4, the brand is on Nagoji's right forearm. The bible's chapter 4 row and the script (3.2, 5.4, 5.5, 6.5) put it only on the inner LEFT forearm.

How I read the arms: Nagoji's chest faces the camera. The torn tunic is open down the front and his face is turned three-quarters toward image-right, showing his right ear with the gold stud. So the shoulder on image-left, where the Fisherman's veined forearm hooks under the armpit, is his RIGHT shoulder. The arm hanging from it, beside the red lungi, is his right arm. Its forearm has branching, raised, reddish-pink ridges just above the bandaged wrist (original px ~430-560, 2050-2300). That is the same shape and placement as the brand in 4.3, where it correctly sits on the image-right (left) forearm. His left arm is not visible anywhere in 4.5, so the only brand on the page after 4.3 is on the wrong arm.

The mark is not too small to matter. It is a vivid red patch on a forearm about a third of an inch long at print size, on the same page as 4.3, and the brand is a plot-critical identifier: "See the brand on his arm" earlier in the chapter, and the Woman fixes her gaze on it in 5.4. It is localized and does not change who the character is, so major, not blocker. Fix: remove the marks from the hanging right forearm and keep only rope chafe under the wrist bandage, or redraw so his left forearm is the one turned toward camera.

One correction to the original report: the bandaged hand gripping across his chest sits at the end of the Fisherman's veined forearm. It reads as the Fisherman's own hand with a bandage, not clearly Nagoji's left hand. That does not change the wrong-arm finding. A Fisherman with a bandaged hand would be a separate minor costume error.

confirmed.description: The hand bandaging changes within the same page. In 3.1 each of Nagoji's fingers is individually wrapped, with the heel of the palm bare, as the script specifies. In 3.4 the bandage covers only his wrists and the backs of his hands, and all the fingers are bare and look healthy. Script: the ruined fingers are never shown directly.
confirmed.evidence: page-03.png, 3.4 original px ~(1250-1530, 2060-2190): the bandages stop at the knuckles and four bare, intact fingers rest on the dhoti. 3.1 original px ~(620-780, 520-590): separately wrapped fingers on both hands.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 3, panel 3.4. I cropped the panel at native resolution, original px ~1100-1700 x 1650-2200. On Nagoji's hand at viewer-left, the bandage covers only the wrist and the back of the hand and stops at the knuckles. Below it, four bare, intact, skin-toned fingers are curled on the dhoti. His other hand is wrapped at the wrist, and the panel's bottom edge cuts it off. Panel 3.1 on the same page (crop ~550-1400 x 450-690) clearly shows each finger capped in its own white wrap on both hands. The script calls for exactly that in 1.2 and 3.1: "the bandage wraps only the fingers". Its notes say "His ruined fingers are never shown directly", and the 5.5 beat depends on the damage being hidden. The CONTINUITY.md row for chapter 4 says nothing about bandages, so nothing there allows bare fingers. Healthy bare fingers contradict both the injury and the rule. At print size the fingers are small, about 0.25 inch, and sit at the bottom edge of the panel. They are still plainly readable as skin against the cream wrap, on the same page where the wrapped fingers are a focal point in 3.1. That makes this a localized costume and continuity error, not something too small to notice. Fix: retouch or inpaint the 3.4 hands so the fingers are wrapped, or crop the hands out of frame. A full redraw is not needed.

confirmed.description: Lettering, outside this lens. The off-panel Wary Fisherman's balloon '<What? He is half dead.>' has its tail pointing into the panel, at the gap just above Nagoji's head. It reads as spoken by Nagoji (or the Fisherman). It should run to the panel edge, toward where the Wary Fisherman stood in 3.4 (off left).
confirmed.evidence: page-03.png, original px: the tail tip is near (993, 2262), directly above Nagoji's hair, with no edge exit.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. On page-03.png, panel 3.5, the tail of the "<What? He is half dead.>" balloon is lettered wrong. The balloon sits in the top-right corner, and its tail runs left and stops in the middle of the panel. The tip is at about (992, 2260) in original pixels, which is mid-panel and nowhere near a border. In a zoomed crop (940-1120 x 2220-2340), the underside of the tail lies right on Nagoji's hair, and the tip is about 10 px from his hairline. If you extend the line of the tail, it points at the Fisherman's head instead. So the tail ties the line either to Nagoji, who is in contact with it, or to the Fisherman, who then seems to answer himself with "<Half is still half.>". Nothing in it marks an off-panel speaker. The script makes this line "WARY FISHERMAN (off)", and neither the script nor the bible allows an in-panel tail here. The fault is easy to see at print size: the panel is about 3.8 in wide and the tail about 0.4 in long, ending on Nagoji's head. Two things soften it: the angle brackets mark the line as Malayalam, which Nagoji doesn't speak, and the third-person "He" helps the reader recover the right speaker. That is why I rate it major rather than blocker. It is a localized speaker-tail error. The fix is to re-letter the tail so it runs to the panel edge (left or top), or to use an off-panel tail treatment.

confirmed.description: The tail on the off-panel Wary Fisherman's balloon "<What? He is half dead.>" points into the middle of the panel and ends just above Nagoji's hair, so it reads as Nagoji speaking. An off-panel voice needs its tail to run to the panel edge (the left, where the Wary Fisherman stood in 3.4). The balloon also sits top-right while the reply "<Half is still half.>" sits top-left only slightly lower, so a reader going left to right can hit the reply before the remark.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed crop: the tail tip sits in open sky about 25 px (display scale) from Nagoji's hairline and about 125 px from the Fisherman's head. No part of the tail reaches toward a panel edge.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on the tail; the reading-order point does not hold up. On page 3, panel 3.5, the off-panel Wary Fisherman's balloon "<What? He is half dead.>" sits top right, directly over Nagoji. Its tail runs left and stops in open sky about 1838,2260 on the full-res page (x≈994). That is about 20 to 30 px (roughly 2 mm at 300 DPI) above and left of Nagoji's hair, and the underside of the tail lies along his curls. The tip is about 640 px (around 54 mm) from the panel's left border, and no part of the tail reaches any panel edge. The script marks this line "WARY FISHERMAN (off)", and the art gives no off-panel cue, so at print size the balloon reads as Nagoji's (or loosely as the Fisherman's, since the tail points toward his head). That is a wrong speaker tail, which the rubric rates major. The fix is local: run the tail to the left panel border, or use an off-panel tail. The words ("He is half dead") make it clear the speaker cannot be Nagoji, which keeps this from being a blocker, but they do not fix the tail. The second claim, about reading order, is weak and should be dropped. The right balloon spans about y 2200 to 2310 and "<Half is still half.>" about y 2295 to 2410. They overlap by only about 15 px, so the right balloon is clearly higher and is read first in normal top-to-bottom order.

confirmed.description: "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." is squeezed into a tall, narrow balloon with one word per line (Come, / bhau. / Before / the / crabs / claim / you.). It reads poorly and looks unlettered next to the other balloons. Its tail stops in the gap right of the Fisherman's beard, directly above Nagoji's hair, so the speaker is unclear. Reflow it to 2 or 3 lines in a wider balloon (there is open sky above the Young Fisherman) and run the tail to the Fisherman's mouth.
confirmed.evidence: Page 4 bottom panel, balloon at about x 485-610, y 1330-1590 (display scale). Seven stacked lines. The tail tip lands between the Fisherman's chin and Nagoji's head.

verdict.reason: The balloon problem is real, but it is minor, not major. On page 4, panel 4.5, "Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you." is set one word per line in a tall, narrow lozenge (about x 670-850, y 1850-2210 at full resolution). It is badly shaped compared with every other balloon on the page, and there is open sky to its right above the Young Fisherman where it could be widened to 2 or 3 lines. That part of the claim holds. Two things lower the severity. (1) Every word is crisp and readable at print size, so this is a shaping and polish fault, not unreadable lettering. (2) The speaker-tail point is weak. The tail runs flat to the left and aims at the Fisherman's beard and chin, the same point the first balloon's tail aims at. Its tip stops in the gap about 7 px above Nagoji's hair, but the direction and the words themselves ("Come, bhau", said to the man being carried) make the speaker clear. A small nudge of the tip up and left, onto the Fisherman's mouth, would remove the leftover doubt. The script (4.5, two FISHERMAN lines) is honored, and nothing in the bible permits or forbids this shaping. Recommended fix: reflow to "Come, bhau. / Before the crabs / claim you." in a wider balloon and move the tail tip onto the Fisherman's mouth.

confirmed.description: The tail on the GIRL's balloon "<Portuguese.>" ends on the back of the head of the second child, who is listening. It should go to the girl with her hand cupped to her mouth, who is whispering. Polish: the line is a whisper but is lettered in a standard solid balloon; a dashed whisper balloon is the usual convention.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of 5.2: the tail tip touches the right-hand child, who is seen from behind. The girl on the left (earring, hand at mouth, facing that child) has no tail pointing to her.

verdict.reason: The art does show it, but it is minor, not major. In 5.2 the tail of the "<Portuguese.>" balloon runs almost flat to the left. Its tip stops on the hair at the back of the right-hand child's head, at about (458, 1070) in the 1838 px page. That child is the listener, seen from behind, and no face is visible. The whisperer is the girl on the left with her hand cupped over her mouth. Her mouth is about 60 px past the tip, roughly 0.2 inch at 300 DPI, hidden behind the listener's head as seen from the balloon. So the tip does land on the wrong child. It is still minor, for three reasons. First, the speaker stays clear: the hand-to-mouth gesture marks the whisperer, and the tail points into that two-child group in the right direction. Second, both children are small girls with earrings, so either reading fits the script's "GIRL" speaker. Third, nothing later depends on it: in 5.3 a single girl in a doorway shrinks back. The fix is quick: route the tail over or past the listener's head to end at the left girl's hand and mouth. The dashed whisper balloon is optional polish, since the script does not ask for one.

confirmed.description: The off-panel line '<What? He is half dead.>' belongs to the WARY FISHERMAN (off), but its tail ends inside the panel between the two visible heads. It reads as if Nagoji, who sits right under the balloon, or the Fisherman says it, which garbles the haggle. The Fisherman would then seem to answer himself with '<Half is still half.>'.
confirmed.evidence: The balloon is at the top right, over Nagoji's head. Its tail points left and stops in open sky beside the Fisherman's ear, well short of the panel edge. It should point off panel, toward the left where the Wary Fisherman stood in 3.4.

verdict.reason: I'm confirming this one as major. On page 3, panel 3.5, the '<What? He is half dead.>' balloon sits at the top right, directly over Nagoji's head. Its tail is a short wedge, about 28pt long, pointing straight left. It stops in open sky between Nagoji's hair and the Fisherman's head, roughly 155pt short of the left panel border. The tail lines up with the Fisherman's head, so the line reads as his. He then seems to answer himself with '<Half is still half.>', and the balloon's position also lets it read as Nagoji's. Nothing on the panel says the speaker is off panel. The script marks this line 'WARY FISHERMAN (off)', and the pipeline's own rule is that a tail to an off-panel speaker runs all the way to the border (reserves.py:514; test_compositor.py test_a_tail_to_an_off_panel_speaker_runs_to_the_panel_border). That test was written for this exact failure in chapter 1 r12 3.1, where a tail stopped short on the man in between and the line read as his. Cause, from review/COMPOSITION-r10.json: the tail target_pt is (85.69, 116.1) and the panel's left clip edge is 83.69pt. The target sits 2pt inside the edge, which misses the 0.5pt off-panel tolerance. The compositor therefore treated the speaker as on-panel and drew a fixed 28pt wedge (tip at 238.5pt). The defect is plainly visible at print size and garbles who says what in the haggle. It is still a wrong speaker tail that a lettering fix can correct without redrawing the art, so major, not blocker.

refuted.description: Ibrahim reads as the tallest man in the room. The bible base line says he is 'shorter than the fishermen but broader', and the script says the Young Fisherman stands just behind him 'half a head taller'. The panel shows the opposite.
refuted.reason:
The finding rests on a premise the art doesn't support. The reviewer says all three men stand on roughly the same floor line. They don't. In panel 6.5, the Young Fisherman's and the Fisherman's feet touch the bottom border at about y=2535. Ibrahim's feet are cut off below it, and his mundu runs past the border. He also overlaps the Young Fisherman's lungi, so he is clearly standing in front, nearer the camera. His face is drawn at about 1.2 times the Young Fisherman's face size, which also shows he is closer.

The script itself asks for this shot: 'Camera low, from beside Nagoji's mat, looking up.' The low camera can be checked in the art. The sea horizon through the doorway sits at about y=2450, around shin height on the standing men. With a level camera, the horizon crosses every standing figure at the same real height, the height of the lens. So you can compare true heights from how far each man's head sits above the horizon against how far his feet sit below it:
- **Young Fisherman:** head about 635 px above, feet about 85 px below, a ratio of about 7.5.
- **Fisherman:** about 565 above and 83 below, a ratio of about 6.8.
- **Ibrahim:** his forehead under the turban is about 650 px above the horizon. His feet are below the border, more than 90 px below. With feet anywhere from about 2545 to 2570, his ratio comes out at about 5.4 to 6.8.

So the geometry fits Ibrahim standing a pace nearer and being the same height as the Young Fisherman or shorter. Measured from the forehead, the turban adds nothing to his real height. His head reaches higher in the frame only because he is nearer the low lens. He is plainly much broader than both fishermen, which the bible line also asks for. The Fisherman is not slim either. He is thick-chested and muscular and stands at about the same depth as the Young Fisherman, just a little shorter.

What remains is a small staging point. The scripted cue that the Young Fisherman stands 'half a head taller' isn't visibly delivered, so a reader can't tell Ibrahim is short. But the art doesn't contradict the bible or the script, so this is at most minor polish, not a major identity error.

refuted.description: A brand-like red ridged patch is drawn on Nagoji's LEFT UPPER ARM, just above the elbow. That is the old 'upper arm' placement which the script's bible change removed (brand = inner left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist). The forearm below it is unmarked, so the upper-arm patch reads as the brand.
refuted.reason: The mark is there, but it is too small and faint to matter in print, so I'm refuting the claim. On page-05.png, panel 5.2, there is a small pinkish ridged mark on Nagoji's left upper arm, roughly x 1015-1035, y 983-993. That makes it about 20x10 px, around 1.7 x 0.85 mm at 300 DPI. It is low contrast: its pixels are about 171/100/84 against skin around it of about 176/116/74, a slight pink shift with no dark outline. In a 1:1 crop (print size) it shows only as a faint spot among the wet-skin highlights. It reads as a brand only when enlarged about 8x. It is also red, while the bible describes the brand as a pale puckered patch. Placement is settled two panels later. In 5.4, where the script puts the brand on show, it is drawn clearly as a pale puckered patch on the inner left forearm above the wrist bandage, as CONTINUITY.md asks. That same panel also shows a purplish bruise or scrape on the same upper arm, so a reader will take the faint 5.2 spot as one of his injuries, not a brand in a second place. 5.2 is a wide village shot whose script does not require the brand to show at all. At most this is optional polish (remove the spot on a future re-render), not a major issue.

refuted.description: Nagoji's uncovered fingers are shown healthy and intact. In 6.4 the left hand has a wrap only at the wrist and across the palm: the fingers are bare and the thumbnail is clean and normal. On the right hand only the middle fingers are wrapped, and the thumb and little finger are bare, which matches neither 3.1 nor 6.5. In 6.5 the left hand's palm is wrapped and its fingers are bare and unharmed, which is the reverse of the established design (fingers wrapped, palm heel bare). Script: the ruined fingers are never shown. The bible's later 'nails healed but ridged' implies damaged nails.
refuted.reason: The art matches the description, but pages 6.4 and 6.5 don't break any design the chapter has actually drawn, so this is not a localized page 6 error. (1) Panel 3.1, the reviewer's own reference, already shows bare fingertips with normal, intact nails. Crops of page-03.png around original px (600-720, 500-600) and (1240-1340, 600-680) show bands on the lower finger segments and clean nails on both hands. The 6.4 right hand repeats that design: bands on the lower segments, bare tips, bare thumb. (2) Panel 3.4 (page-03 ~ (1200-1560, 2020-2190)) already shows the wrist and palm wrapped with the fingers bare, the same look as the 6.4 left hand and the 6.5 left hand. So 6.4 and 6.5 are consistent with earlier pages rather than the reverse of them. (3) In 5.5 the Woman unwinds a bandage and treats him, so a different wrap afterwards is justified in the story. The ch5 bible row only asks for 'hands wrapped in clean linen', and the 6.4 and 6.5 script lines say nothing about the hand wrap. (4) The script's rule that his ruined fingers are never shown directly is a no-gore rule. Bare, unhurt fingertips don't show ruined fingers. In 6.5 the hand is palm up, so only the finger pads show and no nails are visible. (5) The one specific point, a clean left thumbnail in 6.4, is about 20 px wide (roughly 0.07 in at print size) on a hand that isn't the focus of the panel. At print size the hands simply read as bandaged. The underlying gap, that the chapter never shows nail damage, starts on page 3 and runs through the whole chapter. It isn't a page 6 defect.

refuted.description: Anachronism: the kapitan (Ibrahim) is dressed in modern tailoring. He wears a fitted five-button waistcoat with flap patch pockets over a long-sleeved, band-collared, button-front shirt with rolled cuffs. Together they read as a 20th-century Nehru or khadi vest and shirt, not 1740s Malabar dress. The script asks only for 'a pale vest over a white mundu', with no coat.
refuted.reason: The description of the drawing is correct. In page-06.png, bottom tier, the kapitan wears a cream vest with five buttons and two flap patch pockets over a long-sleeved shirt with a band collar and rolled cuffs. But this is the approved design, not a render error. The approved Ibrahim sheet (concepts/09-ibrahim-marakkar-v15.png, listed in APPROVED-SHEETS.json) shows the same outfit: a cream vest with buttons and flap patch pockets ("BULGING VEST POCKETS" is a labelled detail panel), a band-collared shirt with rolled sleeves, a white turban, a white mundu and a striped shoulder cloth. CONTINUITY.md agrees: chapters 4-5 give "Pale vest over a white mundu, no coat", and chapters 6-28 give "Short coat over a vest with bulging pockets." The script allows a pale vest over a white mundu with no coat, and the render follows that. The coat is correctly left out until chapter 6, the white turban and grey-flecked beard are present, and the panel matches the sheet. The vest and shirt cut was approved at sheet level and is carried through the whole book, so it is not a localized error on page 6, panel 6.5. If the author now considers the cut anachronistic, the fix belongs on the character sheet and the bible, not in a redraw of this panel.

refuted.description: The kapitan's build is reversed. The script stages this panel to show that he is shorter than the fishermen but broader, with the Young Fisherman standing just behind him and half a head taller (the bible says the same: 'shorter than the fishermen but broader'). In the art the kapitan is the tallest figure in the frame and no broader than the men behind him.
refuted.reason:
I cropped panel 6.5 on page 6, laid a grid over it and measured. The reviewer's evidence does not hold.

(1) The three men are not at the same depth. The fishermen's feet sit on the bottom border. The kapitan's feet are not shown: his mundu runs off the bottom edge and Nagoji's leg covers it. That puts him a step nearer the low camera.

(2) His head is drawn about 1.4 to 1.5 times the size of the fishermen's heads:
- Eye to chin: about 66 to 70 px for him, about 45 px for each fisherman.
- Face width: about 98 px for him, against 72 and 65 px.

So his apparent height is foreshortening from the low, looking-up camera the script asks for ("Camera low, from beside Nagoji's mat, looking up"). It is not a taller man.

(3) The sea horizon in the doorway, which marks the camera's eye level, sits at about the fishermen's knees. Scaled to that horizon, the kapitan's eye stands well below the Young Fisherman's, so in the scene he is the shorter man.

(4) His shoulders are not narrower. He spans about 380 px across the shoulders against the Fisherman's 215 px. Even scaled down for his nearer depth (about 260 px), he is wider than both fishermen. The art shows him heavy-set and pot-bellied beside two lean men. That is the "broader" the bible and script ask for.

What is left is that the script's direct cue (the Young Fisherman "just behind him, half a head taller") does not read side by side, because the Young Fisherman stands further back. That is at most a staging nicety, and the low camera the script asks for naturally makes the nearest man tower. The build is not reversed.

refuted.description: Wrong speaker tail on the girl's whisper. The script has a small girl whispering '<Portuguese.>' to the child beside her. The tail lands on the listener, not on the girl whispering.
refuted.reason: Refuted. I zoomed into page 5, panel 5.2 at 2x and 3x, and also looked at it reduced to print size. The tail of the '<Portuguese.>' balloon runs almost level from the right and points straight at the face of the girl with her hand cupped to her mouth, the leftmost child. The tip stops on the upper-left of the second child's hair, but that head overlaps and sits directly in front of the girl's face. Any tail coming from the right has to cross it to reach her. The tip is about 55 to 60 px from her nose and cupped hand at 300 DPI, roughly 5 mm on the printed page. The second child faces away from the reader, so we only see the back of her head and nothing shows her speaking. The leftmost girl's cupped hand is an obvious whisper pose. At print size the tail clearly reads as aimed at the whispering girl, so this is not a wrong-speaker tail. If the letterer wants it tighter, they could extend the tip about 5 mm left to her cupped hand. That is optional polish, not a real defect.

minors.description: In the panel meant to fix the fishermen's look for the rest of the chapter, the Fisherman's face already drifts from the 2.1 close-up on the same page. He has a black handlebar moustache, a small grey goatee patch and black hair, where 2.1 gives him a full short grizzled beard.
minors.evidence: Page 2, 2.4, left of the three standing men (red lungi, white cloth on his left shoulder): black curled moustache, grey only at the chin point, cheeks largely clean. In 2.1, directly above on the same page, his full grey-black beard covers his jaw and cheeks.

minors.description: Both fishermen drift in the final panel. The Fisherman is drawn younger and slimmer, with black hair and a mostly black beard, and his plain white shoulder cloth has picked up the blue-striped, fringed border of Ibrahim's sheet shawl. The Young Fisherman is drawn with no beard (thin moustache, bare chin), unlike his chin beard in 2.4, 3.1, 4.5, 5.2 and 5.4.
minors.evidence: 6.5, far right (red lungi): black curly hair, dark beard with only a little grey, lean build, and a white cloth with pale-blue stripes and a fringe exactly like the shawl on Ibrahim beside him. Compare 6.2 on the same page, where the Fisherman is grey-bearded and receding, with a plain white cloth. 6.5, middle (indigo lungi, headband): smooth chin with a thin moustache only, and a softer, younger face.

minors.description: Nagoji's signature small gold ear stud has spread to the fishermen. The Young Fisherman wears one in 4.1 and 4.5, and the Fisherman wears one in 4.1. Neither man has one in any other panel. In 4.5 the Young Fisherman (curly black hair, curled moustache, gold stud) is carrying Nagoji, so the two look-alike traits sit side by side.
minors.evidence: 4.1: a gold bead at the Young Fisherman's left ear, just below the headband knot, and a gold bead on the crouching Fisherman's ear beside Nagoji. 4.5: a gold stud on the Young Fisherman's ear under the trailing end of his headband. No stud appears on either man in 2.4, 3.1, 5.1 to 5.4 or 6.2.

minors.description: The out-of-focus Fisherman in the background wears a gold drop earring, another case of Nagoji's ear-stud marker appearing on a supporting character. It is inconsistent with his other panels.
minors.evidence: 6.4, background left figure (grey beard, white cloth): a small gold drop hangs below his ear, at about the same height as his beard line. He has no earring in 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 or 6.5.

minors.description: The Wary Fisherman loses his gaunt, long-bearded look. In 4.1 his beard is trimmed short and his face looks younger. In 4.5 he has tight grey curls and a heavily muscled, six-pack torso. The scripted character, established in 2.1, 3.3 and 3.4, is older and gaunt, with a long grey-streaked beard and lank hair.
minors.evidence: 4.1, right edge: short neat grey beard, smooth younger face. 4.5, right figure with the net: compact grey ringlets, a broad muscular chest and arms, and a fuller rounded face. Compare 3.3 (page 3, wading at the tide line): a lean, hollow-chested man with a long straggly grey beard and long lank hair.

minors.description: The Woman's face and hair change between her doorway entrance and the washing scene. In 5.4 she has a round, soft face and hair all grey worn loose to the shoulders, with no low knot visible. In 5.5, and again in 6.1, she has a narrower, harder face and darker hair streaked with grey in a low bun. Only the undyed cloth ties the panels together.
minors.evidence: 5.4, right of centre in the doorway: full, rounded cheeks and fully silver hair falling loose around the face and neck. 5.5, right: thinner cheeks, sharper features, dark hair with grey streaks drawn into a bun at the nape. 6.1 (page 6, left) matches 5.5 rather than 5.4.

minors.description: The Fisherman's costume and face drift. His shoulder cloth is now cream with blue stripe bands and a fringe (Ibrahim's sheet cloth), where 2.4, 4.1 and 6.3 show plain white. Blue on his cloth also blurs the colour coding, since blue belongs to the Young Fisherman. His hair and beard are mostly black with grey only at the chin, younger than the grizzled, grey-haired leader of 2.1, 3.4 and 6.3.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, original px ~(1550-1610, 1980-2125): the striped, fringed cloth on the red-lungi man. His face is at ~(1450-1520, 1870-1960). Compare the plain cloth and grey hair in 6.3 at ~(1260-1330, 1080-1260).

minors.description: The Fisherman's white shoulder cloth picks up dark stripe bands near the hem. It is plain white in 2.4, 4.1 and 4.2.
minors.evidence: page-04.png, 4.4 original px ~(1030-1080, 1500-1720): horizontal brownish stripes across the lower cloth.

minors.description: The Fisherman (red lungi, white cloth) does not hold the face set up in 2.1 ('short grizzled beard', held for the chapter). In 5.1 and 5.2 he has black curly hair and a black moustache with only grey stubble on the chin, and reads as a younger man than the grey-bearded, grey-streaked leader of pages 2 to 4 and 5.3.
minors.evidence: page-05.png 5.1 original px ~(500-570, 450-520). 5.2 ~(780-840, 880-960). Compare 5.3 ~(1140-1220, 1270-1340), which has a full grizzled beard.

minors.description: The Woman's look drifts between panels. In 5.4 her hair is almost entirely silver, worn loose and wavy, and her face reads lighter and slimmer. In 5.5 and 6.1 she has dark hair heavily streaked with grey in a low knot, which matches the script. Her drape in 6.1 also gains a dark grey border stripe, against 'coarse undyed cotton'.
The Young Fisherman's headband is dusty pink/mauve here. Everywhere else it is cream/off-white.

The wreck is redesigned and no longer reads as the chapter 2 and 3 ship established in 2.4. In 3.3 it is a low plain hull with bare masts and a bowsprit and no carved stern castle. In 3.5 it is a skeleton of bare ribs that reads as a long-rotted hulk. A squared-masonry wall also appears at the left edge of 3.5, a structure seen nowhere else on this beach.

Settings conflict across the beach pages. In 4.1 the stern-castle ship looms huge and nearly beached just behind the group, where 2.4 and 5.1 put it small and far off on a reef. In 4.5 its masts stand with sails. Also in 4.5, the left background shows a fishing hamlet on the beach (thatched huts, beached boats, nets), which contradicts the empty beach of 2.4 and 5.1, where the village is inland beyond the palms.
minors.evidence: page-04.png 4.1 original px ~(250-830, 390-620): the ship. 4.5 ~(150-350, 2010-2290): the huts and boats. 4.5 ~(1430-1680, 2000-2240): the rigged wreck.

minors.description: Village costume: the foreground girl wears a fitted red short-sleeved blouse, which reads modern. The woman with the maroon waist sash appears to have a pinkish fitted bodice under her drape. The script asks for the village drape with no fitted blouses.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, original px ~(280-420, 1060-1195): the girl's red fitted sleeve. ~(1330-1400, 990-1080): the woman's bodice under the white drape.

minors.description: Ibrahim reads as tall as or taller than the fishermen: the Young Fisherman's head sits level with Ibrahim's eyes. The bible base line says 'shorter than the fishermen but broader', and the script has the Young Fisherman half a head taller.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, original px: the Young Fisherman's head top is ~(1330, 1830) against Ibrahim's eye line at ~(1050, 1830).

minors.description: The brand's design is inconsistent. Here it is four or five thin, pale parallel lines that read like claw scratches. The 3.2 insert and 4.3 establish a puckered, reddish patch of raised ridges.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, original px ~(800-890, 2385-2445), compared with page-03 3.2 and page-04 4.3 ~(720-760, 1680-1780).

minors.description: Nagoji's hands look bare, with no finger bandages. In the very next panel (1.2) both hands are heavily bandaged.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, original px ~(900-960, 600-640) and (1300-1380, 580-640): bare outstretched fingers on the small figure.

minors.description: The lighting jumps. 1.4 is lit by a low golden sun breaking through with rays, and the very next moment (2.1 and all of page 2) is a flat, heavy grey storm sky.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, original px ~(150-950, 2070-2350): a sunburst over the sea. page-02 2.1: an overcast grey sky.

minors.description: The brand on Nagoji's left forearm is drawn as a line of cursive pseudo-script, which counts as pseudo-text painted into the art. It does not read as 'raised ridges blurred past reading'. In 4.5 the same brand becomes a vertical stack of letter-like glyphs, so it also fails to match the rectangular ridged patch in 3.2 and the three dotted ridge lines in 6.5.
minors.evidence: page-04.png panel 4.3, lower right forearm above the wrist bandage, about x 666-902, y 1665-1831 original: pale raised strokes forming joined, letter-like loops. Panel 4.5, the dangling forearm at lower left, about x 416-500, y 2205-2275: stacked glyph-like scar marks.

minors.description: Pseudo-text painted into the art: the carved panels on the wrecked ship's stern castle contain glyph-like shapes, one of which reads as the numeral '3' next to maze-like letterforms.
minors.evidence: page-02.png panel 2.4, the wreck at upper right, stern castle panels at about x 1553-1644, y 1782-1873 original. It is tiny at print size but visible at zoom as a '3' and block glyphs below the stern gallery rail.

minors.description: The kapitan's scar is painted as a thin, bright-red line, so it reads as a fresh bleeding cut rather than an old healed scar. This sits close to the no-blood rule.
minors.evidence: page-06.png panel 6.5, the kapitan's left cheek from below the temple toward the jaw, about x 1040-1096, y 1831-1887 original: a saturated red stroke on the shadowed cheek.

minors.description: Period costume drift: village women and girls wear stitched, fitted short-sleeved blouses or tops. These are anachronistic for 1740s Kerala commoners, and the script calls for women 'modestly covered' with an upper cloth over the mundu and no fitted blouses.
minors.evidence: page-05.png panel 5.2: the background woman at the fence, about x 1234-1332, y 915-1096 original, wears a white short-sleeved blouse or dress with set-in sleeves. The whispering girl in the foreground, about x 277-416, y 1096-1193, wears a fitted red short-sleeved top that reads as a modern t-shirt.

minors.description: The panels on this page have uneven outer edges. Panels 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 and 5.5 are inset to x 167-1158, while 5.3 runs at full width (107-1217), so it sticks out about 60 px past every other panel on both sides. The approved Chapter 1 pages keep one consistent outer frame, and their narrower panels differ by about 15-20 px at most.
minors.evidence: Pixel scan of the left and right panel edges at y 400, 740, 1350 and 1700 gives 167/1158. At y 1000 (5.3) it gives 107/1217.

minors.description: The top tier is misaligned. The top border of 6.2 sits about 10 px (display scale) lower than the top of 6.1, and its bottom border about 9 px higher, so the two panels do not share a top line or a bottom line.
minors.evidence: Pixel scan: 6.1 top at y 258, 6.2 top at y 267.5 (display scale). The bottoms are visibly offset in the 6.1/6.2 crop.

minors.description: The balloon "She says keep your stories for the kapitan." touches both the top and right panel borders, and "She does not need to hear them to know what kind of men they are." touches the bottom border. Tangent balloons look cramped. Chapter 1 insets its balloons from the frame.
minors.evidence: In the crop, the right edge of the first balloon is about 2 px from the panel's right border line, and its top meets the top border. The bottom of the second balloon sits on the bottom border.

minors.description: Across the chapter, caption boxes are butted flush against the panel border lines with no inset. The Chapter 1 standard insets captions about 10-15 px from the frame. Examples: 1.1 (top edge), 1.2 and 1.3 (top-right corner), 2.1 and 2.4 (top corners), 4.3 (top-right), both captions in 5.1 (top and bottom edges), 6.4 (top-right), 6.5 (top-left).
minors.evidence: In Chapter 1 r6 page 1, the caption "The first thing they took was my name." sits about 15 px inside the panel's top-left corner. Here, the 1.1 caption's top edge is the panel border itself.

minors.description: The second caption, "After the dungeon and the storm, these small things felt like gifts.", covers the torso and net of the Wary Fisherman, who leads the carry party. It also sits right on the bottom border. Shrink it and move it into the foliage at lower left, or tuck it below his figure.
minors.evidence: The caption box spans about x 643-1040, y 515-608 (display scale), over the Wary Fisherman's chest and net. Its bottom edge meets the panel border.

minors.description: Awkward crop: the top border cuts Nagoji's face just below the eyes, so only his nose, moustache and ear stud show above the torso. The cut reads like a framing accident rather than a choice, and the caption is jammed into the corner beside it.
minors.evidence: Crop of the top of 1.2: the panel's top line runs across the bridge of his nose, and neither eye is visible.

minors.description: The heads of the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman are jammed against the top border; the Fisherman's hair is clipped. The caption "I recognised the curve of a Portuguese hull." is wedged against the Fisherman's head at top left. The full-figure panel needs more headroom.
minors.evidence: Crop of 2.4: the top of the Fisherman's head meets the border at about x 550-600, and the Young Fisherman's headband nearly touches it. The right edge of the caption box sits a few px from the Fisherman's hair.

minors.description: The large balloon "I know they have not yet learned to kneel when a foreign flag flies." covers the lower-left half of the two-shot, including Nagoji's propping elbow and arm. The script's beat is that he is still propped on one elbow with his back straight. The balloon's bottom also nearly sits on the panel border.
minors.evidence: Crop of 4.4: the balloon spans about x 708-985, y 1135-1315 (display scale), over Nagoji's arm and the Fisherman's knee. Its bottom edge is about 4 px from the border.

minors.description: The boy's untranslated balloon reads "~~ kapitan ~~ / kapitan ~~", with a few typographic tildes as the only filler. It reads as sing-song rather than "a rush of unreadable speech (broken wavy strokes)". The script asks for scribble strokes filling the balloon around the two clear words.
minors.evidence: The 6.2 balloon contains only four tilde pairs and two italic "kapitan" words, with a lot of empty space around them.

minors.description: The kapitan's costume goes beyond the script's 'pale vest over a white mundu, no coat'. He wears a long-sleeved, band-collared shirt with rolled cuffs under a four-button waistcoat with flap pockets. The full sleeves read as a jacket, which blurs the chapter 6 coat reveal, and the outfit looks modern.
minors.evidence: White full sleeves are visible on both arms under the cream vest, and the vest has two flap pockets at the hips. A blue-striped towel over his shoulder is also unscripted.

minors.description: The staging drifts from the beat. The script asks for a tight, ground-level shot of his hands dug into the grit while he lies spent ('My limbs felt like they belonged to someone else'). The art shows him up on all fours with straight, muscular arms, as if crawling out under his own power. It also shows his lower face, moustache and ear stud, before the 1.3 close-up, and he is face-down again in 1.3.
minors.evidence: In the panel he is braced on locked arms with his torso lifted off the sand. His lower face, moustache and gold stud are visible at the top of the frame.

minors.description: The light change overshoots and breaks continuity. The script wants the light 'shifted' to show time passing, but the very next panel (2.1) asks for 'a lowering grey sky'. Here a golden sunset with sunbeams sits between two grey storm skies.
minors.evidence: There is a bright orange sun with radiating rays at the upper left of 1.4. Every panel on page 2 has a dark grey overcast sky.

minors.description: The rope loops have vanished from his chest one panel early. The script has them still on him in 2.2 and cut away on camera in 2.4. The water is also poured from above rather than the pot being 'pressed to his cracked lips'.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's chest and tunic at the bottom of 2.3 show no rope. The clay pot is held a hand's length above his face, with a stream falling into his open mouth.

minors.description: The order of the carry party is wrong. The script has the Wary Fisherman leading the climb (he 'wants to be anywhere else', and in 4.5 he is already walking ahead). Here he trails at the rear, downhill of the others, and the caption box half covers him.
minors.evidence: The Fisherman with the shoulders is uphill at the far left, and the Young Fisherman is in the middle. The Wary Fisherman, with the net, is lowest and rightmost, and his torso is behind the 'After the dungeon...' caption.

minors.description: The script calls for 'low houses of mud and red laterite stone with palm-thatch roofs'. The background houses on the right have clay-tile roofs, which is also doubtful for a 1738 fishing village.
minors.evidence: Behind the women with water pots, at the upper right of the panel, two houses have ridged terracotta tile roofs. Only the foreground house on the left is thatched.

minors.description: The script beat is that the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman 'exchange a look across the room' when the boy says 'kapitan', a silent sign that they know who he is. In the art they sit side by side and both turn toward the boy, so the shared look is lost.
minors.evidence: Both men are at the right of the panel, shoulder to shoulder, and both heads are turned left toward the doorway.

minors.description: Nagoji's posture jumps. The panels on either side have him lying on the mat (6.3 looking up at the Fisherman, 6.5 reclining and opening his eyes). In 6.4 he sits bolt upright, cross-legged, in a meditative pose. The panel is also inset from the margins, although the script says 'Full-width tier'. Panel 4.1, scripted as 'Wide, full width', is inset the same way.
minors.evidence: In 6.4 he sits upright, cross-legged, with his hands on his knees. The borders of 6.4 and 4.1 sit about 27 px (display scale) inside the margins of the full-width panels around them.

minors.description: This is the panel meant to establish the three fishermen 'at full figure' for the rest of the chapter, but the top border crops the heads of the two leading men.
minors.evidence: The Fisherman's head is cut off at the forehead and the Young Fisherman's hair is clipped by the top border. The caption box butts against the Fisherman's face.

minors.description: The lettering in the balloon 'Come, bhau. Before the crabs claim you.' is set in a tall, narrow column of one or two words per line, which reads awkwardly.
minors.evidence: In the centre balloon the line breaks run: 'Come, / bhau. / Before / the / crabs / claim / you.'

minors.description: In the brand insert, the forearm has a heavy black ink outline that matches no other render in the chapter. It reads like a compositing seam.
minors.evidence: A thick black line runs down both edges of the forearm, from the top of the panel to the bandage, most visibly the curve along the right side of the arm.
